PHYS 101.description: A practical introduction to physics and science in everyday life-from concrete examples to basic physical principles.
PHYS 101.subject: PHYS
PHYS 101.title: The Physics of How Things Work I

PHYS 101L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 101 .
PHYS 101L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 101L.title: The Physics of How Things Work I Lab

PHYS 102.description: A continuation of PHYS 101 with emphasis on electricity, magnetism, optics, and atomic physics.
PHYS 102.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 101.
PHYS 102.subject: PHYS
PHYS 102.title: The Physics of How Things Work II

PHYS 102L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 102 .
PHYS 102L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 102L.title: The Physics of How Things Work II Lab

PHYS 151.description: The physics of sound, color, illumination; musical instruments and photographic processes. Credit may not be received for both PHYS 151 and PHYS 153 or both PHYS 151 and PHYS 155 .
PHYS 151.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151.title: Physics in the Arts

PHYS 151L.description: Laboratory work on wave motion, including acoustic, optical, photographic, and electronic measurements. Credit may not be received for both PHYS 151L and PHYS 153L or both PHYS 151L and PHYS 155L .
PHYS 151L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151L.title: Physics in the Arts Laboratory

PHYS 153.description: Principals of optics: video, and photography, eye and vision, color, polarization, lasers, and holography. Credit may not be received for both PHYS 153 and PHYS 151 .
PHYS 153.subject: PHYS
PHYS 153.title: Physics in the Visual Arts

PHYS 153L.description: Laboratory work in geometrical and wave optics. Credit may not be received for both PHYS 153L and PHYS 151L .
PHYS 153L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 153L.title: Physics in the Visual Arts Laboratory

PHYS 155.description: The principles of musical and architectural acoustics, waves and vibrations, digital techniques for generating and recording sound, perception and measure of sound (psychoacoustics). Credit may not be received for both PHYS 155 and PHYS 151 .
PHYS 155.subject: PHYS
PHYS 155.title: Musical Acoustics

PHYS 155L.description: Laboratory work in musical and architectural acoustics. Credit may not be received for both PHYS 155L and PHYS 151L .
PHYS 155L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 155L.title: Acoustics Laboratory

PHYS 199.description: Measurements in classical and modern physics are performed, and the analyzed results are compared with basic principles. Four hours of mixed lecture and laboratory per week.
PHYS 199.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 115 or equivalent or higher.
PHYS 199.subject: PHYS
PHYS 199.title: Measurement and Analysis in Physics

PHYS 201.description: First part of an introductory course sequence. Topics include mechanics, and selections from wave motion, sound, fluids, and heat. No previous background in physics is assumed.
PHYS 201.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 111, MATH 111I, MATH 112, MATH 115, MATH 116, MATH 122, MATH 141, or by placement score into MATH 122, MATH 141, or higher.
PHYS 201.subject: PHYS
PHYS 201.title: General Physics I

PHYS 201L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 201 .
PHYS 201L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 201L.title: General Physics Laboratory I

PHYS 202.description: Continuation of PHYS 201 ; includes electromagnetism, and selected topics from optics, relativity, quantum physics, atomic and nuclear physics.
PHYS 202.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 201.
PHYS 202.subject: PHYS
PHYS 202.title: General Physics II

PHYS 202L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 202 .
PHYS 202L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 202L.title: General Physics Laboratory II

PHYS 211.description: Classical mechanics and wave motion. Calculus-level course for students of science and engineering.
PHYS 211.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 141.
PHYS 211.subject: PHYS
PHYS 211.title: Essentials of Physics I

PHYS 211L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 211 .
PHYS 211L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 211L.title: Essentials of Physics I Lab

PHYS 212.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 211 and MATH 142.
PHYS 212.subject: PHYS
PHYS 212.title: Essentials of Physics II

PHYS 212L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations to accompany PHYS 212 .
PHYS 212L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 212L.title: Essentials of Physics II Lab

PHYS 291.description: Special theory of relativity. Algebra-based course for students of all majors.
PHYS 291.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in MATH 115 or equivalent.
PHYS 291.subject: PHYS
PHYS 291.title: Einstein’s Relativity: Understanding by Example

PHYS 306.description: Wave motion, optics, and thermodynamics. Calculus-level treatment; a continuation of PHYS 212 .
PHYS 306.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 212 and MATH 142.
PHYS 306.subject: PHYS
PHYS 306.title: Principles of Physics III

PHYS 307.description: Experimental foundations and general concepts of quantum theory and special relativity; with selected applications from atomic, condensed matter, and nuclear physics.
PHYS 307.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 212 and MATH 241.
PHYS 307.subject: PHYS
PHYS 307.title: Introduction to Modern Physics

PHYS 310.description: Descriptive statistics, scientific ethics, and design, construction, and reporting the results of experiments.
PHYS 310.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 212 and STAT 509 or STAT 515.
PHYS 310.subject: PHYS
PHYS 310.title: Intermediate Experimental Physics

PHYS 311.description: Introduction and application of linear algebra and numerical methods to the solution of physical and engineering problems. Techniques include iterative solution techniques, methods of solving systems of equations, and numerical integration and differentiation.
PHYS 311.subject: PHYS
PHYS 311.title: Introduction to Applied Numerical Methods

PHYS 340.description: Final states of stellar evolution; white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes. Cosmology.
PHYS 340.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ASTR 201; C or better in MATH 115; C or better in PHYS 202 or PHYS 212.
PHYS 340.subject: PHYS
PHYS 340.title: Introduction to Relativistic Astrophysics

PHYS 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
PHYS 399.subject: PHYS
PHYS 399.title: Independent Study

PHYS 498.description: An individual investigation in the library or laboratory or both under supervision of the major professor. The preparation of a scientific report is an integral part of the work.
PHYS 498.subject: PHYS
PHYS 498.title: Senior Thesis

PHYS 499.description: Introduction to and application of the methods of research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester.
PHYS 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 310.
PHYS 499.subject: PHYS
PHYS 499.title: Undergraduate Research

PHYS 501.description: A self-contained treatment of quantum theory and its applications, beginning with the Schrodinger equation.
PHYS 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 307 and MATH 242 or MATH 520.
PHYS 501.subject: PHYS
PHYS 501.title: Quantum Physics I

PHYS 502.description: Advanced topics in quantum physics, plus topics in special relativity, high-energy physics, and cosmology.
PHYS 502.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 501.
PHYS 502.subject: PHYS
PHYS 502.title: Quantum Physics II

PHYS 503.description: Classical mechanics of particles, systems, and rigid bodies; discussion and application of Lagrange's equations, introduction to Hamiltonian formulation of mechanics.
PHYS 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 306 or PHYS 307 and MATH 242 or MATH 520.
PHYS 503.subject: PHYS
PHYS 503.title: Mechanics

PHYS 504.description: Field theory of electric and magnetic phenomena; Maxwell's equations applied to problems in electromagnetism and radiation.
PHYS 504.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 503.
PHYS 504.subject: PHYS
PHYS 504.title: Electromagnetic Theory

PHYS 506.description: Principles of equilibrium thermodynamics, kinetic theory, and introductory statistical mechanics.
PHYS 506.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 306, PHYS 307, MATH 241 and MATH 242 or MATH 520.
PHYS 506.subject: PHYS
PHYS 506.title: Thermal Physics and Statistical Mechanics

PHYS 511.description: An elementary treatment of nuclear structure, radioactivity, and nuclear reactions. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
PHYS 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 501.
PHYS 511.subject: PHYS
PHYS 511.title: Nuclear Physics

PHYS 515.description: Analytical function theory including complex analysis, theory of residues, and saddlepoint method; Hilbert space, Fourier series; elements of distribution theory; vector and tensor analysis with tensor notation.
PHYS 515.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 242 or MATH 520.
PHYS 515.subject: PHYS
PHYS 515.title: Mathematical Physics I

PHYS 516.description: Group theory, linear second-order differential equations and the properties of the transcendental functions; orthogonal expansions; integral equations; Fourier transformations.
PHYS 516.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 515.
PHYS 516.subject: PHYS
PHYS 516.title: Mathematical Physics II

PHYS 517.description: Application of numerical methods to a wide variety of problems in modern physics including classical mechanics and chaos theory, Monte Carlo simulation of random processes, quantum mechanics and electrodynamics.
PHYS 517.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 212 and MATH 142.
PHYS 517.subject: PHYS
PHYS 517.title: Computational Physics

PHYS 520.description: An introduction to the physical principles that underlie a variety of important biological and biophysical phenomena. Combines both physical and biological perspectives to explore a wide range of topics not possible in stand-alone undergraduate physics- or biological-science courses. Designed to be suitable for both bio-oriented and physics-oriented students.
PHYS 520.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211; C or better in MATH 141; C or better in BIOL 101.
PHYS 520.subject: PHYS
PHYS 520.title: Introduction to Biological Physics

PHYS 541.description: Continuation of PHYS 310 . Optical apparatus (telescope, microscope, interferometer) and advanced project planning including equipment design and budgeting.
PHYS 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 310.
PHYS 541.subject: PHYS
PHYS 541.title: Advanced Experimental Physics I

PHYS 542.description: Continuation of PHYS 541 . Study of topics from advanced optics, astronomy, biophysics, digital electronics, nuclear/particle physics, or solid state physics, plus conduction of a physics experiment, including a written paper and an oral presentation.
PHYS 542.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 541.
PHYS 542.subject: PHYS
PHYS 542.title: Advanced Experimental Physics II

PHYS 546.description: The basics of observational techniques, structure and evolution of stars, interstellar medium and star formation, structure and properties of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, and generation and transfer of radiation in astrophysical environments.
PHYS 546.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 307 or graduate student standing.
PHYS 546.subject: PHYS
PHYS 546.title: Introduction to Astrophysics

PHYS 599.description: Readings and research on selected topics in physics. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHYS 599.subject: PHYS
PHYS 599.title: Topics in Physics

PHYS 700.description: Understanding physics students; current teaching methods supported by research in physics, physics education, education, psychology, and cognitive science.
PHYS 700.subject: PHYS
PHYS 700.title: Seminar on Teaching Learning in Physics Astronomy

PHYS 701.description: Generalized coordinates, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations, variational principles, transformation theory, and Hamilton-Jacobi equation.
PHYS 701.subject: PHYS
PHYS 701.title: Classical Mechanics

PHYS 703.description: Development of classical fields; Maxwell's equations; boundary value problems; radiation theory.
PHYS 703.subject: PHYS
PHYS 703.title: Classical Field Theory I

PHYS 706.description: Statistics of Boltzmann, of Fermi and Dirac, and of Bose and Einstein, with applications.
PHYS 706.subject: PHYS
PHYS 706.title: Statistical Thermodynamics

PHYS 708.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of general relativity and a discussion of problems of current interest.
PHYS 708.subject: PHYS
PHYS 708.title: General Relativity and Cosmology

PHYS 711.description: A development of non-relativistic quantum mechanics.
PHYS 711.subject: PHYS
PHYS 711.title: Quantum Mechanics I

PHYS 713.description: Second Quantization. Relativistic formulations of quantum mechanics.
PHYS 713.subject: PHYS
PHYS 713.title: Advanced Quantum Theory

PHYS 714.description: Theory of quantized fields. Introduction to renormalization. A continuation of PHYS 713 .
PHYS 714.subject: PHYS
PHYS 714.title: Quantum Field Theory

PHYS 721.description: Nuclear physics, mainly from the experimental standpoint.
PHYS 721.subject: PHYS
PHYS 721.title: Subatomic Physics

PHYS 723.description: Introduction to elementary particles. The quark model. Symmetry principles and conservation laws. Calculation of cross sections and decay rates using Feynman rules. Accelerators, particle detectors, and experiments.
PHYS 723.subject: PHYS
PHYS 723.title: Elementary Particles I

PHYS 724.description: Experimentally accessible processes and their description using the framework developed in PHYS 723 . Gauge theories and the standard model. Particle experiments for the next decade and their underlying physics descriptions.
PHYS 724.subject: PHYS
PHYS 724.title: Elementary Particles II

PHYS 725.description: The crystalline state of matter and its main characteristics. Electric and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators.
PHYS 725.subject: PHYS
PHYS 725.title: Solid State Physics

PHYS 726.description: Theory and description of conventional and high temperature superconductors and their properties.
PHYS 726.subject: PHYS
PHYS 726.title: Superconductivity

PHYS 727.description: Basic theory. Electron spin resonance. High resolution and wideline nuclear magnetic resonance. MÃƒÂ¶ssbauer effect. Magnetic resonance and dielectric relaxation.
PHYS 727.subject: PHYS
PHYS 727.title: Magnetic Resonance

PHYS 728.description: Semi-classical and fully quantum-mechanical treatments of interactions between matter and electromagnetic fields on the microscopic level.
PHYS 728.subject: PHYS
PHYS 728.title: Quantum Optics - Understanding Light-Matter Interactions

PHYS 729.description: Groups and representations. Full rotational group. Angular momentum. Ligand field theory. Application to atomic, molecular, and nuclear physics.
PHYS 729.subject: PHYS
PHYS 729.title: Applied Group Theory

PHYS 730.description: Presentation by the student of a designated topic. May be repeated for credit.
PHYS 730.subject: PHYS
PHYS 730.title: Graduate Seminar

PHYS 731.description: Extragalactic astrophysics, including nearby and distant galaxies, active galaxies, galaxy clusters, large-scale structure, galaxy formation/evolution, scale structure, galaxy formation/evolution, basics of cosmology, cosmic radiation backgrounds, and observation constraints on cosmological models.
PHYS 731.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: PHYS 701, PHYS 703, and ASTR 211 or equivalent.
PHYS 731.subject: PHYS
PHYS 731.title: Extragalactic Astrophysics

PHYS 739.description: Obtain necessary skills and habits needed to work in any research group by performing hands-on experiments including finding a collaborator, researching the literature, performing the experiment, analyzing data, interpreting/understanding the results, and writing a report.
PHYS 739.subject: PHYS
PHYS 739.title: Graduate Research Laboratory

PHYS 740.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHYS 740.subject: PHYS
PHYS 740.title: Selected Topics in Physics

PHYS 743.description: Fundamentals of quantum information processing, including quantum computation, quantum algorithms, quantum cryptography, and basic quantum information theory. Topics include: the quantum circuit model, alternative models, qubits, unitary operators, measurement, entanglement, quantum algorithms for factoring and search, quantum cryptographic key distribution, simulation of physical systems, error-correction and fault-tolerance, quantum channels, complexity of quantum computation, near-term implementations, quantum computer programming.
PHYS 743.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 344, MATH 544, or MATH 700, or the equivalent, or instructor permission.
PHYS 743.subject: PHYS
PHYS 743.title: Quantum Computer Science

PHYS 745.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHYS 745.subject: PHYS
PHYS 745.title: Topics in Nuclear Physics

PHYS 746.description: This is an astrophysics course for physics graduate students. The course will cover the basics of observational techniques, structure and evolution of stars, interstellar medium and star formation, structure and properties of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, and generation and transfer of radiation in astrophysical environments.
PHYS 746.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C+ or better in PHYS 307, PHYS 503, PHYS 506.
PHYS 746.subject: PHYS
PHYS 746.title: Principles of Astrophysics

PHYS 750.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHYS 750.subject: PHYS
PHYS 750.title: Topics in Solid State Physics

PHYS 755.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHYS 755.subject: PHYS
PHYS 755.title: Topics in Theoretical Physics

PHYS 760.description: Introduction to and the application of the methods of research.
PHYS 760.subject: PHYS
PHYS 760.title: Research

PHYS 761.description: Introduction to and the application of the methods of research.
PHYS 761.subject: PHYS
PHYS 761.title: Research

PHYS 764.description: Fundamentals of quantum information theory and quantum communications. Topics include: Postulates of quantum mechanics, classical information and entropy, compression of classical information and classical typical sets, quantum entropy and quantum relative entropy, quantum states discrimination, Schumacher's theory of quantum compression and quantum typical subspace, communicating classical information using quantum channels, the Classical Capacity Theorem of a quantum channel.
PHYS 764.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 344 or MATH 544 or equivalent, or permission by the instructor; and C or better in MATH 511 or STAT 511 or equivalent, or permission by the instructor; knowledge of quantum mechanics is not required.
PHYS 764.subject: PHYS
PHYS 764.title: Quantum Information
